h1: The 6 Best 75-Inch TVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 6 best 75-inch TVs of 2026, covering Samsung Mini-LED, Neo QLED, QLED and Crystal UHD plus an LG Nano set.
summary: The Samsung QN90F Neo QLED is the best 75 inch TV on this list because it holds the highest panel tier. The M80H and M70H bring Mini-LED backlighting for less money, the QN70H is the QLED value pick, and the U8000H is the simple 4K option. LG's NU85 is the alternative if you prefer its brand and sound features.
intro: At 75 inches, a television stops being a gadget and becomes a wall feature, and every flaw scales up with it. Uneven backlighting, washed out blacks and thin sound are all easy to ignore on a bedroom set and hard to ignore across a living room. Panel technology is the lever that matters most here.

Six sets made the ranking, five from Samsung and one from LG. Two 85 inch models were dropped because they do not match the size in the title. The listings reveal little beyond panel type and series name, so our editors ordered the sets by panel tier first and series position second.

products.name: Samsung 75-Inch Class Neo QLED 4K QN90F Series
products.verdict: The highest panel tier of the Samsung sets in this ranking.
products.description:
The Samsung QN90F is a 75 inch Neo QLED 4K set, and its listing places it in the $500+ bracket. Neo QLED is the top panel tier among the Samsung sets here, which is the single reason it leads. A big premium screen suits a large living room where brightness and contrast are put to work.

It ranks first ahead of the Mini-LED M80H because Neo QLED sits one tier above in Samsung's own lineup. The gap to the M80H is small, though, and the M80H may cost less, so this is a ranking of panel tier rather than a runaway win.

Buy it for a big, bright room where you want the best panel on the list. The caveat is thin listing detail: beyond series and panel name, there is little to compare, so confirm the current price and features on the product page.
products.idealFor: Large living rooms that want a premium panel.
products.skipIf: You are on a tight budget.

products.name: Samsung 75-Inch Class M80H Series
products.verdict: A 75 inch Mini-LED in the higher M-series.
products.description:
Samsung's M80H is a 75 inch Mini-LED set, and the listing names the panel but shows few other specifics. Mini-LED uses a more refined backlight than basic LED sets, which is why it earns a high slot.

It takes second place because the M80H sits above the M70H in series number, so it gets the first call among the two Mini-LED models. It trails the QN90F on panel tier, but the distance is modest. Against the QN70H below, the Mini-LED backlight is the clear step up.

It fits buyers who want Mini-LED at this size and a higher series number than the M70H. One caveat is that no price bracket appears on the listing, so look up the current price before comparing it with the M70H, which does list one.
products.idealFor: Mini-LED buyers who want the higher series.
products.skipIf: You want a stated price bracket.

products.name: Samsung 75-Inch Class M70H Series
products.verdict: The Mini-LED M70H lists in the $500+ bracket.
products.description:
The Samsung M70H is another 75 inch Mini-LED set, and its listing shows the $500+ bracket. It shares the backlight technology of the M80H, which puts it ahead of every QLED and Crystal UHD model on the list.

It lands third because it sits one step under the M80H by series number. Compared with the QN70H below, the Mini-LED panel is the reason to pay more, though the listing offers little more than panel and size to prove it.

This is a sensible first large screen with Mini-LED technology, especially if the M80H price is higher in your market. Skip it if you want the top M series. The honest limit is sparse detail, so verify features such as ports and smart platform on the listing.

products.name: Samsung 75-Inch Class QN70H Series
products.verdict: A 75 inch QLED set below the Mini-LED models.
products.description:
Samsung's QN70H is a 75 inch QLED set, and the listing gives the panel name and little more. QLED is a clear step above plain LED in this lineup, which keeps it comfortably above the Crystal UHD model.

It sits fourth because QLED ranks below Mini-LED in our order. The jump from the M70H is a backlight difference, not a size difference, so the picture trade is real but not dramatic for casual viewing. Against the U8000H, you gain the QLED panel for what is likely a modest step in cost.

Pick it for a bright room on a mid range budget when Mini-LED feels like overkill. The caveat is that no price bracket is shown, so check pricing before you commit.
products.idealFor: Bright rooms on a mid-range budget.

products.name: Samsung 75-Inch Class U8000H Series Crystal UHD
products.description:
The Samsung U8000H is a 75 inch Crystal UHD 4K set, the entry panel in this group. The listing mentions no QLED or Mini-LED technology, so you are buying size and 4K resolution rather than premium picture tech.

It ranks fifth because Crystal UHD sits below QLED in our order. It stays above the LG NU85 mainly on brand familiarity and a simpler lineup position, not on a spec advantage the listings can prove.

It suits casual viewers who want a very large screen for sports, news and streaming without paying for a premium panel. Skip it if you watch movies in a dark room. The caveat is the entry level panel, and the listing shows no price bracket, so confirm it before buying.

products.name: LG 75-Inch Class Nano AI 4K NU85 Series Smart TV w/AI Sound Pro
products.verdict: The only non-Samsung set, with Nano tech and AI Sound Pro.
products.description:
LG's NU85 is the only non-Samsung TV here, a 75 inch Nano 4K smart set with AI Sound Pro, listed in the $500+ bracket. The audio feature is its main differentiator, since big thin TVs usually ship with small speakers.

It comes last because Nano is a lower panel tier than QLED or Mini-LED, and the listing's price bracket suggests you are not saving money to get it. Against the U8000H, you gain a smart platform and sound processing, but not a clearly better panel.

Choose it if you prefer LG's interface or want improved built in audio. Skip it if picture quality is the priority. The caveat is that there is no Mini-LED or OLED option from LG in this ranking.
products.idealFor: LG fans who want a big screen.

whatMatters.detail: Panel technology is the display type behind the picture. Mini-LED and Neo QLED use finer backlighting, while Crystal UHD is the entry tier. It matters because contrast and brightness drive how a large screen looks in your room. Find the panel name in the listing title, and compare tiers within one brand.

Viewing distance is how far your seat sits from the screen. A 75 inch 4K set suits roughly 8 to 10 feet, and sitting closer can make individual pixels visible. Measure from your sofa to the wall before buying, and make sure the room can take a screen this wide.

Stand and wall fit decide whether the TV works in your space. A 75 inch set is wide, and the feet may sit farther apart than your furniture allows. Check the stand dimensions, weight and mounting pattern on the manufacturer page, and plan to anchor a wall mount into studs.

Built in audio matters because thin panels leave little room for speakers. Features such as the LG's AI Sound Pro help, but a soundbar still beats any internal set. Look for audio features in the title, and budget for a separate speaker if you watch a lot of movies.

Series naming tells you where a model sits inside a brand. Samsung's M80H outranks the M70H, and QN-prefixed sets use different panels from the U-prefixed Crystal UHD line. Compare series within one maker rather than across brands, and read the panel name on the listing instead of trusting the number alone.

howToChoose.intro: Panel tech matters most in how bright your room is.

cards.label: Mini-LED
cards.text: A backlight of many small LEDs. The M70H and M80H.

cards.label: QLED
cards.text: Quantum dot color, simpler backlight. The QN70H and the Neo QLED QN90F.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to Mini-LED or Neo QLED if the budget allows.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A panel that holds up in ambient light and 4K resolution.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Samsung QN90F is our pick, with the M80H second.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The room is bright or you watch a lot. The QN90F and M80H justify it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You watch casually. The U8000H is the simplest set here.

faq.a: About 8 to 10 feet suits a 75 inch 4K set such as the Samsung QN90F or M80H. Closer than that, you may notice pixel structure, and farther back you lose some of the immersion a large screen offers.
They do not match the 75 inch size promised in the title, and a buyer comparing the QN90F with an 85 inch set would be misled on room fit and cost. We kept the list to true 75 inch models.

faq.q: Is Mini-LED worth it over QLED?
faq.a: On paper, yes. Mini-LED sets such as the Samsung M80H and M70H use a more refined backlight than QLED models like the QN70H, so they are the step up. The listings give few other specs, so judge by panel tier.

faq.q: How do I mount a 75 inch TV?
faq.a: Check the weight and mounting pattern on the manufacturer page, then anchor the bracket into wall studs. A 75 inch set like the Samsung U8000H or LG NU85 is wide and heavy, so consider a second person for the lift.

Most likely. Thin 75 inch sets, including the LG NU85 with AI Sound Pro, have small speakers compared with their screen size. A soundbar is a common add and gives dialogue and bass a clear improvement for movies.

faq.q: Why do some listings lack a price bracket?
faq.a: The listing data for some Samsung sets, such as the M80H, QN70H and U8000H, did not include one. Check the current price on the product page before comparing against the QN90F, M70H or LG NU85, which show the $500+ bracket.

finalTake: Buy the panel, not the badge. The QN90F is the set to choose if the budget stretches, and the Mini-LED M80H is the smart step down. The QN70H and U8000H make sense for casual viewing in brighter rooms, and the LG NU85 suits buyers loyal to that brand. Check the current price on each listing, since several lack a bracket.
